title: UIC Richard J. Daley Library, third floor — rooms 3190F / 3190G+H / 3190J
anchor: pen 18'11" G+H interior width (IMG_7594) — also the PDF-vector scale anchor
interpretations: 3190G and 3190H are modeled as ONE room: pen note on IMG_7594 says the partition was removed by the contractor and a bulkhead will be in its place 8'3" above the floor. Pen beats print (Benton, 31 Aug 2026).
The 17'3" on IMG_7594 is the clear width BETWEEN the two 10" heaters, not the room width — the chain 10" + 17'3" + 10" = 18'11" closes exactly. Recorded as parts of run 0.

On IMG_7595 the 8'10" is a VERTICAL chain along 3190J's door wall — north corner to the door's near jamb, with the 38" door below it (Benton's corner->jamb convention). It is not a second width; the two pen widths do not disagree.

3190F's two widths (9'3" mid-room, 9'6" at the door wall) are 3" apart; the print linework shows the east wall stepping out where the heater ends, so F is modeled with a 3" jog at 9'1" from the back wall. CONFIRM with Gabe — if the two chains were meant to be the same span, one is a misread.

winding.reason: walked counter-clockwise on purpose, and declared so it cannot be mistaken for a mirrored read: the only MEASURED door position on this job is the vertical pen chain on IMG_7595, which runs north corner -> near jamb down the west (corridor) wall. A clockwise walk from the northwest corner would put that wall's run travelling north from the south corner, forcing the pen 8'10" to be restated as a subtraction (14'4" - 8'10" - 38") and turning the one hard number on the job into arithmetic. Geometry is unchanged; only the starting corner and travel direction differ.
